subject: Post-call recap: ShipWise throughput signature & streaming handoff
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@shipwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: ShipWise throughput signature & streaming handoff

Elena — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and clearly defined next steps so we can size a pilot and propose the right Dedicated footprint.

High-level workload notes (from call):
- Endpoint: conversational routing + streaming partial responses to browser clients.
- Steady-state: ~60 QPS (avg request rate) with median payload ~340 tokens/request.
- Peak: ~420 QPS sustained for a 6–12 minute crest during end-of-day processing (approx 7x steady multiplier).
- Per-request behavior: majority (≈70%) are streaming interactions with incremental token flushing; tail-latency sensitive.
- Target SLO: 95th <= 250 ms for non-stream token latency; interactive streaming flushes acceptable up to ~500 ms for the first partial chunk.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent sessions ~1.8k, peak concurrent sessions ~12k.

Questions / clarifications we need to finalize sizing:
1) Can you share a 24‑hour traffic trace (CSV or pcap-like export) with timestamps + tokens/request distribution and streaming chunk sizes? (Link preferred to Drive).
2) Confirm the percent of requests that are multi-turn (you mentioned ~45% keep the session open >30s) — is that accurate?
3) Any hard constraints on cold-start latency for new sessions or auth-proxy hops we should budget for?
4) Do you need request-level persistence for audit (token logs) vs. only aggregated telemetry?

Proposed immediate next steps / owners:
- Alex: Consolidate sizing assumptions and produce a preliminary tokens/sec & GPU-hour estimate (deliverable by EOD tomorrow).
- Marissa: Prepare a pilot checklist (data controls, sample eval prompts, success criteria).
- Elena / ShipWise: Share traffic trace and confirm go‑live target window.

Attachments: shipwise_slo_matrix.xlsx (blank template attached), call-recording-20270928.mp3 (link).

Thanks — I’ll follow-up with a quick estimate once I have the trace.

—Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Torres <elena@shipwise.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: ShipWise throughput signature & streaming handoff

Thanks Alex — this is helpful and captures the call. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 42O QPS peak is tied to our batching job that fires at 6:45pm PST; it usually lasts ~8–10 minutes and is primarily write-heavy (but still triggers streaming responses for a subset of flows).
- Multi-turn stat: yes, ~45% continue after the first response for another turn; about 25% of those do another subsequent turn.
- We can share a sanitized 48-hour trace (CSV) with per-request token counts and a column for whether the request used streaming. Will upload to Drive by tomorrow morning.
- For auditing: we retain request IDs and response hashes, but we cannot export full token text — aggregated telemetry is fine for sizing.

Looping in Samir (platform) who will provide the trace and confirm retention constraints.

Elena Torres
Head of Product, ShipWise
elena@shipwise.com

Elena / Alex — great notes. A couple of operational points from CS/solutions: 

- For streaming-heavy workloads we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for stable conversation starters — that will cut token work for repeated prompts by ~18–25% in our experience. We'll include a config sketch in the pilot checklist.
- Batching settings: with your reported token distributions, an adaptive micro-batching policy (batch target ~64 tokens or 8 ms fill window) gives the best cost/latency tradeoff. We’ll prototype in the pilot.
- Audit/telemetry: since ShipWise cannot export full token text, we’ll instrument aggregated token-by-minute histograms + per-route 95th token latency. That matches Redwood Optimize signals.

Karthik — can you produce a first-cut Dedicated footprint (GPUs, expected tokens/sec capacity, and planned autoscale policy) using the assumptions in Alex’s note + the 7x peak multiplier? We need something to share in the solutions deck.

Action items:
- Marissa: Pilot checklist + suggested eval prompts (today).
- Karthik: Preliminary footprint estimate (this morning if possible).
- ShipWise: Drive link to traces and any sample env for test harness.

—Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

Quick sizing note (preliminary, ballpark — will refine after trace):

Assumptions (from thread):
- Steady QPS: 60 qps * 340 tokens/request = ~20.4k tokens/sec steady
- Peak crest: 420 qps * 340 = ~142.8k tokens/sec (approx 7x steady) sustained ~10 minutes
- Streaming overhead: assume +15% token processing overhead due to chunking and session handling

Adjusted tokens/sec: 
- Steady: ~23.5k tokens/sec (including overhead)
- Peak crest: ~164k tokens/sec

GPU sizing (very rough):
- For interactive latency SLOs (~95th <=250ms) with streaming, a mixed fleet: 2x A100-80GB-equivalents for steady traffic with autoscale headroom to add 6 additional cards for peak crests (hot-add via burst pool). That provides sustained throughput with room for caching benefits and batching windows.
- If ShipWise prefers to avoid burst pool complexity, recommend a Dedicated 8x 80GB commit for peak coverage.

Open asks (need from trace to finalize):
1) Exact token-size distribution (we need percentiles: p50/p90/p99 tokens per request).
2) Streaming chunk sizes (avg first-chunk tokens + subsequent chunk sizes).
3) Concurrency profile alignment (we used your concurrent session numbers to sanity-check memory/KV cache sizing).
4) Any SLA requirements for cold-start or per-request auth handshake durations.

Next: I’ll convert this into a short slide with cost/commit options and the tradeoffs (burst pool vs committed Dedicated) — posting to the HubSpot deal + share Drive folder. Can we book a 30-min follow-up tomorrow 11am PT to walk the deck?

—Karthik Iyer
Capacity & Performance, Redwood Inference
